mainTopic: Payment for a miscarriage (דמי ולדות): when an ox's owner pays, how the loss is valued, and who receives it
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about someone who causes a pregnant woman to miscarry. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says to appraise the babies and pay the husband, and the משנה exempts the attacker when the woman was a freed maidservant or a convert. The גמרא shows that an ox's owner is exempt from דמי ולדות even when the ox aimed at the woman, but רב פפא says he pays when the woman is a שפחה, because she counts like property. The גמרא then explains how the payment is measured, and רבה and רבא give two readings of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's objection, each backed by a ברייתא. The two ברייתות are reconciled: a woman having her first child is worth more after birth, while another woman is worth more while pregnant. The extra word ״הרה״ teaches the רבנן that the pregnancy's added value goes to the husband, while רבן שמעון בן גמליאל uses it to require a blow near the womb. Finally, רבה limits the exemption for a convert's wife to a blow while her husband was alive, רב חסדא disagrees, and a ברייתא brought against רבה gets one answer here and a second answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל objects: the woman is worth more after birth
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל attacks the first opinion's method of valuing the miscarriage by pointing out that a woman is worth more after giving birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then once a woman gives birth she goes up in value!
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of the משנה. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is challenging the first opinion's way of calculating the payment for the lost babies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion said to compare the woman's value while pregnant with her value after birth. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל objects that this method does not work, pointing to how birth changes her value. The גמרא later gives two different readings of his short objection: רבה's in step 11 and רבא's in step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: an opening that attacks an opinion by showing its result does not work

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: He means: if we value the loss the way the first opinion said, comparing her worth while pregnant with her worth after birth.

phrases.english: once the woman gives birth, she increases in value!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from the previous daf, attacking the first opinion's valuation method.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first opinion's method of valuing the miscarriage by the woman's value before and after birth
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A woman is worth more after birth than while pregnant, so that comparison would show no loss and make the payment meaningless.

steps.title: Appraise the babies and pay the husband or his heirs
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's own method: value the babies themselves, and the payment goes to the husband, or to his heirs if he has died.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we estimate how much the babies would have been worth, and he gives that to the husband. And if she has no husband, he gives it to the husband's heirs.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the first method, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gives his own: put a value on the babies themselves. He also says who gets the money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of measuring a change in the woman's value, the court values the lost babies directly. The money belongs to the husband, and if he has died, it goes to his heirs. That the money goes to the husband sets up the next ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: We appraise or estimate the value

phrases.english: Rather, we appraise the offspring:
how much they are worth,
and he gives it to the husband.
And if she has no husband,
he gives it to his heirs.
phrases.notes: 'His heirs' means the husband's heirs, since the money really belongs to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שָׁמִין אֶת הַוְּלָדוֹת כַּמָּה הֵן יָפִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a replacement method after the objection in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Value the babies directly. Payment goes to the husband, or to his heirs if he has died.

steps.title: A freed maidservant or a convert: the one who caused the damage is exempt
steps.stepSummary: If the woman was a freed maidservant or a convert, the one who caused the miscarriage pays nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she had been a maidservant and was freed, or she was a convert, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a case where nobody collects the payment for the babies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The payment goes to the husband or his heirs, not to the woman. If the husband had no heirs, there is nobody entitled to collect. So the one who caused the damage is exempt.
steps.confusionAlert: The exemption does not come from her being a freed maidservant or convert in itself. It follows from the previous line: the money belongs to the husband, so if he has died with no heirs, nobody can claim it.

phrases.english: If she was a maidservant and was freed,
or a convert, he is exempt.
phrases.notes: This builds on the line before: the money goes to the husband's heirs, so if he died with none, nobody is left to collect.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיְתָה שִׁפְחָה וְנִשְׁתַּחְרְרָה, אוֹ גִיּוֹרֶת – פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule from step 2, that the money goes to the husband or his heirs, to a case where nobody can collect.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If nobody is entitled to the payment, the one who caused the damage is exempt.
steps.whatToRemember: דמי ולדות belong to the husband or his heirs, not to the woman. When there is no one to receive them, nobody pays.

steps.title: Does the משנה's wording refute רב אדא בר אהבה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the משנה that an ox that meant to gore the woman would make its owner pay דמי ולדות. This seems to contradict רב אדא בר אהבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The reason he is exempt is that the ox meant to gore another ox. That implies that if it meant to gore the woman, he pays for the babies. Shall we say this refutes רב אדא בר אהבה? For he said: oxen that meant to gore the woman are exempt from paying for the babies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It draws an inference from an earlier line of the משנה and uses it to challenge רב אדא בר אהבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said an ox that was aiming at another ox and hit the woman is exempt from דמי ולדות. Reading carefully, the exemption seems to depend on the ox aiming elsewhere, so an ox aiming at the woman would be liable. But רב אדא בר אהבה says even oxen that aimed at the woman are exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason, used to draw an inference from the exact wording
But, which implies that... (introduces the opposite case)

phrases.english: Gemara: The reason is that it was intending to gore its fellow,
phrases.notes: This points back to the earlier line of the משנה: an ox aiming at another ox that hit the woman doesn't pay for the babies.

phrases.english: but if it was intending to gore the woman,
he pays compensation for the offspring.
Shall we say this is a refutation
of Rav Adda bar Ahava?
For Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
Oxen that intended to gore the woman
are exempt from compensation for the offspring?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא תֶּיהְוֵי תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה to the גמרא. It goes back to an earlier line of the משנה, about an ox aiming at another ox, and draws an inference from it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא בר אהבה's ruling that oxen that aimed at the woman are exempt from דמי ולדות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's wording suggests the exemption depends on the ox aiming at another ox. So an ox aiming at the woman would be liable, which contradicts רב אדא בר אהבה.

steps.title: The משנה's wording only matches the next case about people
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה could answer that oxen are always exempt. The משנה said 'aiming at another' for the ox only to match the next case about people, which follows the wording of the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה could say to you: the same is true even if the oxen aimed at the woman; they are also exempt from paying for the babies. The משנה taught 'an ox that was aiming at another' only because it wanted to teach the next case, 'a person who was aiming at another,' since that is how the פסוק is written. So it taught the first case in the same way: 'an ox that was aiming at another.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב אדא בר אהבה. It explains that the משנה's wording does not imply what the challenge assumed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inference only works if the phrase 'aiming at another' was chosen on purpose for the ox case. The answer is that it was not. The פסוק (שמות 21:22) describes men fighting with each other and hurting the woman, so the סיפא about people uses that wording, and the רישא about oxen was phrased the same way to match it. Oxen are exempt from דמי ולדות either way.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you: introduces a possible defense
Since, because of: wording chosen to match another clause

steps.whatToRemember: When wording in the רישא is copied from the סיפא for consistency (אַיְּידֵי), we do not draw an inference from it. רב אדא בר אהבה's ruling stands: oxen are exempt from דמי ולדות even when they aimed at the woman.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לְךָ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava could say to you:
The same is true, that even
if they intended to gore the woman,
they are also exempt from compensation for the offspring;
and as for what it teaches:
'An ox that was intending to gore its fellow,'
since it wants to teach the latter clause:
'A person who was intending to strike his fellow,'
since that is how the verse is written,
it also teaches the first clause in that way:
'An ox that was intending to gore its fellow.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: הוּא הַדִּין דַּאֲפִילּוּ נִתְכַּוְּונוּ לָאִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4 by taking away the basis for its inference.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The wording is explained as chosen to match the next clause (אַיְּידֵי), so no inference can be drawn from it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase 'aiming at another' in the ox case was chosen on purpose, which implies an ox aiming at the woman makes its owner pay.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ox case copies the wording of the people case, which follows the פסוק. Oxen are exempt from דמי ולדות either way.

steps.title: An ox that gores a maidservant does pay for her babies
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that if an ox gores a שפחה and she miscarries, the owner pays דמי ולדות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא says: if an ox gored a maidservant and her babies came out, the owner pays for the babies.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a new ruling: when an ox gores a שפחה and she miscarries, the ox's owner must pay for the babies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5 we learned that an ox's owner normally does not pay דמי ולדות. רב פפא says there is an exception when the woman is a שפחה. The reason comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives this ruling
Payment for babies lost in a miscarriage

phrases.english: Rav Pappa says:
An ox that gored the maidservant,
and her babies came out,
he pays compensation for the babies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to the rule from step 5 that an ox's owner does not pay דמי ולדות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An ox that gores a שפחה and causes a miscarriage makes its owner pay דמי ולדות.

steps.title: The reason: a maidservant counts like property
steps.stepSummary: The ox simply damaged property, like a pregnant donkey. The proof is a reading of 'עם החמור' as 'עַם הדומה לחמור'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? The ox just damaged a pregnant donkey, so to speak. The פסוק says 'Stay here with the donkey,' and this is read as 'a people similar to a donkey.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רב פפא's ruling. For this law a שפחה counts like an owned animal, so the ox damaged property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exemption for oxen covers harm to a person. A Canaanite slave is legally treated like her master's property, so this case is plain property damage, like hurting a pregnant donkey. The פסוק is read in a play on words, turning עִם ('with') into עַם ('a people').

keyTerms.meaning: A people similar to a donkey

steps.confusionAlert: This is a legal category about ownership and damages. It is not a statement about a person's worth as a human being.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
It merely damaged a pregnant donkey,
as the verse says:
"You stay here with the donkey"
a people that is similar to a donkey.
phrases.notes: The word עִם ('with') is read as if it said עַם ('a people').

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? חֲמָרְתָּא מְעַבַּרְתָּא בְּעָלְמָא הוּא דְּאַזֵּיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason and the source for רב פפא's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's ruling that the owner pays for a שפחה's babies
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 22:5, 'עם החמור', read as 'עַם הדומה לחמור'
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains why the exemption for oxen from step 5 does not apply here. The case is treated as property damage, not harm to a person.

steps.title: Why does the משנה call it 'payment for babies'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה. The method described measures the woman's increase in value, so it should be called שבח ולדות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה asks, 'How does he pay for the babies?' But is that the right name? It should have said 'the increase from the babies'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה. It complains that the name of the payment does not match the method the משנה describes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion compares the woman's value before and after birth. That measures how much the pregnancy raised her value, which is שבח ולדות. So why call it דמי ולדות, a payment for the babies themselves?

keyTerms.meaning: The increase in the woman's value because of the babies

phrases.english: "How does he pay compensation for the babies?"
"Compensation for the babies"?!
It should have said "the increase from the babies"!

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד מְשַׁלֵּם דְּמֵי וְלָדוֹת. ״דְּמֵי וְלָדוֹת״?! ״שְׁבַח וְלָדוֹת״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רב פפא and returns to the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The method described measures an increase in value, so the payment should be called שבח ולדות, not דמי ולדות.

steps.title: The משנה means both payments
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means both דמי ולדות and שבח ולדות. The appraisal before and after birth measures the שבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is what it means: how does he pay for the babies and also for the increase from the babies? They appraise how much the woman was worth before giving birth and how much she is worth after.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about two payments together. The before-and-after appraisal is the part that measures the increase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase in the משנה is treated as shorthand for 'דמי ולדות and שבח ולדות.' The babies' value is paid, and so is the drop in the woman's value. The before-and-after comparison measures that drop.

keyTerms.meaning: This is also what it is saying

phrases.english: This is also what it is saying:
How does he pay compensation for the babies
and the increase from the babies?
They appraise the woman:

phrases.aramaic: כַּמָּה הִיא יָפָה עַד שֶׁלֹּא יָלָדָה,
phrases.english: how much she is worth before she gave birth,
and how much she is worth after she gave birth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the משנה's phrase as including more than it states outright
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה describes only one payment, so its name does not fit.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means both דמי ולדות and שבח ולדות, and the appraisal measures the שבח.

steps.title: What did רבן שמעון בן גמליאל mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's objection from the משנה and asks what exactly he meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: If so, once a woman gives birth she goes up in value! What is he saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's short objection from the משנה. His words are unclear, so it asks what he meant, setting up רבה's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His words 'once a woman gives birth she increases in value' are short and puzzling. How does that disprove the first opinion's method? The גמרא wants his argument spelled out.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces a problem with the other view)

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
If so,
once a woman gives birth she increases in value!
What is he saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the first opinion's method, the גמרא turns to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's objection to it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's short objection

steps.title: רבה explains: a woman is worth more after birth
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that a woman is worth more after birth than before. So the before-and-after method fails, and the babies themselves should be appraised.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said, this is what he means: Is a woman worth more before birth than after? Isn't she worth more after birth than before? So instead, they appraise the babies and give the money to the husband.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה spells out רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's argument. The first method would find no loss at all, so we must value the babies directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion assumes a pregnant woman is worth more and that the miscarriage lowered her value. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says it is the opposite: she is worth more after giving birth. So comparing before and after shows no loss, and the babies themselves must be appraised.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who explains רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's words
They give the money to the husband

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה's reading of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, a woman is worth more after birth. So the payment is based on the value of the babies themselves, and it goes to the husband.

phrases.english: Rabba said, this is what he is saying:
But is a woman worth more before she gives birth
than after she gives birth?
But isn't a woman worth more after she gives birth
than before she gives birth!
Rather, they appraise the babies,
and give the money to the husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He means that a woman is worth more after birth, so the before-and-after method shows no loss. Instead, the babies are appraised and the money goes to the husband.

steps.title: A ברייתא teaches the same explanation
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא states רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's argument in exactly the same words as רבה, which supports רבה's explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is also taught this way: Is a woman worth more before birth than after? Isn't she worth more after birth than before? So instead, they appraise the babies and give the money to the husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with the same wording as רבה. This shows that רבה's explanation is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's reading was his own explanation of a short statement. Now a תנאי source says the same thing word for word, so his explanation is confirmed.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also taught this way (in a ברייתא), bringing support

steps.whatToRemember: רבה's explanation of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is confirmed by a ברייתא: value the babies and give the money to the husband.

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
But is a woman worth more before she gives birth
than after she gives birth?
But isn't a woman worth more after she gives birth
than before she gives birth!
Rather, they appraise the babies
and give the money to the husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבה's explanation from step 11 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's explanation of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the same wording

steps.title: רבא's different explanation: pregnancy raises the woman's value
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains רבן שמעון בן גמליאל differently: a pregnant woman is worth more because of the pregnancy itself. So the babies go to the husband, and that extra value is split between husband and wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: this is what רבן שמעון בן גמליאל means. Does the woman gain value only for her husband, and get nothing herself from the value the babies add? Rather, the court appraises the babies and gives that to the husband, and the husband and wife split the added value from the babies.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second answer to the question from step 10, what did רבן שמעון בן גמליאל mean? His answer is different from רבה's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said a woman is worth more after birth, so the before-and-after method fails. רבא says the opposite: pregnancy makes her worth more, beyond the value of the babies themselves. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's complaint is that the first תנא gives that extra value only to the husband, but she deserves a share. So the babies' value goes to the husband, and the שבח ולדות is divided.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he is teaching, introducing a reading of a source
They divide, split it between them

steps.confusionAlert: רבה and רבא say opposite things about the facts. רבה says she is worth MORE after birth. רבא says pregnancy makes her worth MORE while pregnant. Keep the two apart.

phrases.english: Rava said: This is what he is teaching:
phrases.notes: "He" is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. רבא reads his words in the משנה differently than רבה did.

phrases.english: But does the woman increase in value only for the one for whom she gives birth,
phrases.notes: "The one she gives birth for" means her husband.

phrases.english: and she herself has nothing at all in the increase from the offspring?
Rather, they appraise the offspring
and give it to the husband,
and the increase in value from the offspring, they divide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, competing answer to the question of step 10, alongside רבה's answer in step 11
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What did רבן שמעון בן גמליאל mean in his objection in the משנה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Pregnancy raises the woman's value. The babies are appraised for the husband, and the extra value is split between husband and wife.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבא's explanation
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the same words רבא used. It adds that damage and pain are appraised separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is also taught this way: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said, does the woman gain value only for her husband, and get nothing herself from the added value of the babies? Rather, damage is appraised by itself and pain by itself. The babies are appraised and given to the husband, and the added value from the babies is split.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches רבא's explanation word for word, to support him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as step 12 brought a ברייתא for רבה, here a different ברייתא backs רבא. This ברייתא also says the woman's own injury payments, נזק and צער, are figured separately. The sharing is only about the extra value from pregnancy.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way, introducing a supporting ברייתא
Damage, the loss in value from the injury

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
But does the woman increase in value only for the one for whom she gives birth,
and she herself has nothing at all in the increase from the offspring?
Rather, they appraise damage by itself,
phrases.notes: These are the woman's own payments for being hurt, and they belong to her.

phrases.english: and pain by itself;
and they appraise the offspring and give it to the husband,
and the increase in value from the offspring, they divide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's explanation from step 13 with a ברייתא that uses his exact words
steps.raayaObject: רבא's reading that pregnancy raises the woman's value and the extra is divided
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in רבא's exact words

steps.title: The two ברייתות of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא (step 12) has רבן שמעון בן גמליאל saying a woman is worth more after birth. The other (step 14) has him saying pregnancy makes her worth more. These clash.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a contradiction between רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the two ברייתות quote the same תנא saying opposite things, and it challenges this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות were brought as proofs, one for רבה and one for רבא. But they cannot both be right about the same woman. Is she worth less while pregnant, or more? The גמרא needs to explain how one תנא could hold both.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a contradiction between one statement and another

phrases.english: There is a difficulty: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's statement
contradicts Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's statement!

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשְׁיָא דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אַדְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the ברייתא of step 14 against the ברייתא of step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ברייתות quoting רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One says pregnancy lowers her value compared to after birth. The other says pregnancy raises her value. The same תנא cannot hold both about the same case.

steps.title: No contradiction: first birth versus later births
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתות speak about different women. One is a woman having her first child, who is worth less while pregnant. The other is a woman who has given birth before, whose pregnancy raises her value.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here it speaks of a woman giving birth for the first time; there it speaks of a woman who is not giving birth for the first time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by splitting the cases: each ברייתא is about a different kind of woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A first birth is riskier, so a pregnant woman having her first child is worth less until she gives birth safely. That is the ברייתא that matches רבה. A woman who has given birth before is not seen as at the same risk, so her pregnancy adds value. That is the ברייתא that matches רבא. So רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is consistent.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult, there is no contradiction
A woman giving birth for the first time
Here ... there, assigning each source to a different case

steps.whatToRemember: רבה and רבא both explain רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, each supported by a ברייתא. They fit together because a first-time mother is worth more after birth, while a woman who has given birth before is worth more while pregnant.

phrases.english: It is not difficult;
here it is about a woman giving birth for the first time,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא from step 12. A first birth is riskier, so she is worth less until she gives birth.

phrases.english: there it is about a woman who is not giving birth for the first time.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא; כָּאן בִּמְבַכֶּרֶת, כָּאן בְּשֶׁאֵינָהּ מְבַכֶּרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source refers to a different situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות speak about the same pregnant woman, so they contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first-birth ברייתא says she is worth more after birth. The later-birth ברייתא says pregnancy raises her value. Both views of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל are consistent.

steps.title: What is the source for the רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the רבנן say that even the value the pregnancy adds goes to the husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, who say that even the added value from the babies goes to the husband: what is their reason?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view is explained, the גמרא turns to the רבנן and asks for their source. This sets up the next step, which brings a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן give the husband both the babies' value and the extra value the pregnancy adds to the woman. The גמרא wants to know what Torah source gives the husband that extra amount too.

keyTerms.meaning: The added value that comes from the babies

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, who say
that the added value from the babies also goes to the husband
what is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן דְּאָמְרִי שְׁבַח וְלָדוֹת נָמֵי לַבַּעַל מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view, the גמרא turns to the other side of the argument.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for the רבנן giving the pregnancy increase to the husband.

steps.title: The extra word 'pregnant' gives the increase to the husband
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק already says the babies came out, so the word ״הרה״ is extra. It teaches that the pregnancy increase goes to the husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: since the verse says 'and her babies come out,' don't I already know she is pregnant? So why does it say 'pregnant'? To tell you that the increase from the pregnancy goes to the husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that reads the word ״הרה״ in the פסוק as an extra word with its own lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If her babies come out, she obviously was pregnant, so the Torah did not need to say ״הרה״. The extra word teaches that the value the pregnancy adds to the woman also belongs to the husband.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the verse need to say this?
The added value that comes from the pregnancy

steps.whatToRemember: For the רבנן, the extra word ״הרה״ gives the husband even the value the pregnancy adds to the woman.

phrases.english: As we learned: from what is implied by the verse saying
'and her babies come out'
don't I already know that she is pregnant?
So why does the verse say 'pregnant'?
To tell you: the increase from the pregnancy goes to the husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the source for the רבנן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra word ״הרה״ teaches that the pregnancy increase belongs to the husband.

steps.title: What does רבן שמעון בן גמליאל learn from 'pregnant'?
steps.stepSummary: If רבן שמעון בן גמליאל does not give the pregnancy increase to the husband, what does he do with the extra word ״הרה״?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: what does he learn from this word 'pregnant'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what lesson רבן שמעון בן גמליאל takes from the extra word, since he does not use it the way the רבנן do. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word that seems extra must teach something for everyone. Since רבן שמעון בן גמליאל splits the pregnancy increase, he must use ״הרה״ for some other lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he learn from it?

phrases.english: And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
what does he learn from this word 'pregnant'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הַאי הָרָה מַאי דָּרֵישׁ בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the other side uses the same extra word.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבן שמעון בן גמליאל learns from ״הרה״.

steps.title: Liable only when he strikes near the womb
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל uses ״הרה״ for רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's rule: the attacker pays for the babies only if he struck her opposite the womb.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what was taught in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: he is never liable unless he strikes her opposite the womb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל uses ״הרה״ to teach where the blow must land for the attacker to pay for the babies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״הרה״ points to the part of her body that holds the pregnancy. So he is liable for losing the babies only when the blow lands on that area.

phrases.english: He needs it for what was taught in a ברייתא:
Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:
he is never liable
unless he strikes her opposite the womb.
phrases.notes: He is talking about paying for the lost babies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers what רבן שמעון בן גמליאל learns from ״הרה״.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״הרה״ teaches that he is liable only for a blow opposite the womb.

steps.title: רב פפא: any spot where the blow can reach the baby
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that 'opposite the womb' means any place where the blow's force can reach the baby. It does not include a hand or foot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Don't say exactly opposite the womb. Rather, anywhere the effect of the blow reaches the baby. This excludes a hand or foot, which do not count.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא clarifies how wide the 'womb area' is in רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is not about one exact spot. It covers any place where the blow could affect the baby, but a blow to a hand or foot does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: The effect of the blow (its heat or bruise)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: לָא תֵּימָא כְּנֶגֶד בֵּית הֵרָיוֹן מַמָּשׁ,
phrases.english: Don't say exactly opposite the womb,
rather, any place
where the effect of the blow reaches the baby.
This excludes a hand or foot, which do not count.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא כְּנֶגֶד בֵּית הֵרָיוֹן מַמָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the key term in the rule quoted in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any blow whose effect can reach the baby counts. A blow to a hand or foot does not.

steps.title: רבה: the exemption applies only if the husband died after the blow
steps.stepSummary: The משנה exempts the attacker when the woman is a freed maidservant or a convert. רבה limits this to a blow while her convert husband was alive. If the blow came after he died, she gets the payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she was a maidservant who was freed, or a convert, he is exempt. רבה said: This was taught only when he hurt her while the convert was alive, and then the convert died. Since the blow came in the convert's lifetime, the convert acquired the payments. Once the convert died, the attacker acquires them from the convert. But if he hurt her after the convert died, she acquires them, and he must pay her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה, and רבה explains when this exemption really applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the convert husband lived, the payment became his. When he died, his property became ownerless, so the attacker, who is holding the money, keeps it. If the blow came after the husband died, the right to the payment starts out as hers, so the attacker must pay her.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of

steps.confusionAlert: The גֵּר here is the woman's husband, not the woman. The money is only lost because a convert who dies with no Jewish heirs leaves his property ownerless.

phrases.english: If she was a maidservant who was freed,
or a convert, he is exempt.
Rabba said: This was taught only
when he hurt her while the convert was alive,
phrases.notes: The convert here is her husband.

phrases.english: and then the convert died;
since he hurt her while the convert was alive,
the convert acquired them (the payments),
and once the convert died,
he (the attacker) acquires them from the convert.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל חָבַל בָּהּ לְאַחַר מִיתַת הַגֵּר –
phrases.english: But if he hurt her after the convert died,
she herself acquires them,
and he must pay her herself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁחָבַל בָּהּ בְּחַיֵּי הַגֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The exemption applies only if the blow came before the convert husband died. If it came after, the woman collects.

steps.title: רב חסדא: with no husband, nobody collects for the babies
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rejects רבה's idea. The payment for the babies is not an object she holds. The Torah gives it only to a living husband, so with no husband there is no payment at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Master of this ruling! Are the babies bundles of money, that she acquires them? Rather, if there is a husband, the Torah gives it to him. If there is no husband, no one gets it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא sharply disagrees with רבה's claim that the woman collects when the blow comes after her husband died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה treated the babies' value like property the woman could take over. רב חסדא says it is a special Torah payment for the husband only. So if the husband is not alive, the attacker owes nothing for the babies, even if the blow came after the husband died.

keyTerms.meaning: Master of this ruling! (a cry of surprise)

steps.whatToRemember: רבה: if the blow came after the convert husband died, the woman collects. רב חסדא: the Torah gives the babies' payment only to a husband, so with no husband nobody collects.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the payment for the babies is not ordinary property. It is a right the Torah gives only to the husband.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: Master of this ruling!
phrases.notes: This is a cry of surprise, as if to say: how could anyone say this?

phrases.english: Are the babies bundles of money
that she acquires them?!
Rather, if there is a husband,
the Torah gives it to him;
if there is no husband, no one gets it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבה's ruling that the woman collects after her husband's death.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבה's ruling that the woman collects when the blow came after her convert husband died.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The babies' value is not property she can take over. The Torah gives it only to a living husband.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to say the convert's wife gets nothing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: the attacker pays damage and pain to the woman and the babies' value to the husband or his heirs. But if she was a freed maidservant or a convert, the attacker keeps the money. This seems to go against רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: If someone hit a woman and she lost her babies, he pays for damage and pain to the woman, and the value of the babies to the husband. If the husband is not alive, he pays his heirs. If the woman is not alive, he pays her heirs. If she was a maidservant who was freed, or a convert, the attacker keeps the money!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to attack רבה's rule that the woman gets the payment for the babies if the blow came after her convert husband died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that for a freed maidservant or a convert, the attacker 'acquires' the money, meaning he pays nothing. It does not split between a blow before or after the husband died. That sounds like no payment at all, which fits רב חסדא and goes against רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged, by bringing a source that seems to contradict
Payment for the injury itself and for the pain
Payment for the value of the lost babies
He acquired. Here it means the attacker keeps the money and pays nothing

phrases.english: They challenged:
If he hit the woman, and her babies came out,
he gives damage and pain payments to the woman,
and the value of the babies to the husband.
If there is no husband, he gives it to his heirs,
if there is no woman, he gives it to her heirs.
If she was a maidservant and was freed, or a convert,
he acquires!
phrases.notes: The attacker gets to keep the money, so nobody is paid for the babies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source against רבה, supporting what רב חסדא said in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's rule that the woman gets the payment if the blow came after the convert husband died.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says flatly that with a freed maidservant or convert, the attacker keeps the money. It makes no split for a blow after the husband died.

steps.title: Read the ברייתא like the משנה: the blow came while the husband was alive
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is no stronger than the משנה. The משנה was already explained as a blow during the convert's life, and the ברייתא can be explained the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Is the ברייתא any better than our משנה, which we explained as a case where he hurt her while the convert was alive, and then the convert died? Here too, he hurt her while the convert was alive, and then the convert died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבה by reading the ברייתא the same way רבה read the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה also said the attacker is exempt, and רבה already limited it to a blow while the husband was alive. The ברייתא says the same thing, so it can be limited in the same way. That means it does not cover a blow after the husband died, which is the case where רבה says she is paid.

keyTerms.meaning: We set it up, meaning we explained it as a specific case
During the lifetime of the convert husband

phrases.english: They said:
And is it better than our משנה,
which we explained as where he hurt her during the convert's lifetime,
and then the convert died?

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי – שֶׁחָבַל בָּהּ בְּחַיֵּי הַגֵּר,
phrases.english: Here too, it is where he hurt her during the convert's lifetime,
and then the convert died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24 by limiting the ברייתא to a narrower case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא), the same way the משנה was limited
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא denies payment even when the blow came after the husband died.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא, like the משנה, is about a blow while the husband was alive. The convert acquired the payment, and when he died with no heirs it became ownerless, so the attacker, who is holding it, keeps it. A blow after the husband's death, where רבה says she collects, is not covered by the ברייתא.

steps.title: A second answer begins: even after the husband died
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts another answer: the ברייתא may even be talking about a blow after the convert died. The explanation of how this fits continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: it is after the convert died,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a second, different answer to the challenge. The rest of this answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer does not limit the ברייתא to a blow during the husband's life. It accepts that the case may be a blow after his death. So the גמרא will have to read the ברייתא's words in a way that still fits רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say, introducing another answer
After the death of the convert

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a full answer yet. Do not decide what it means until you see how the גמרא finishes it on the next amud.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
after the death of the convert,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second way to answer step 24's challenge, instead of the limitation given in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative answer that keeps the ברייתא about a blow after the husband's death (finished on the next amud)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The only way to save רבה is to limit the ברייתא to a blow during the husband's life.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even a blow after the husband's death can be fit into the ברייתא. The details come on the next amud.
